images.seen: A man in a beanie and scarf walking a small terrier along the Sea Point promenade at night, lampposts glowing, cloud pouring over Lion's Head, dark calm sea. Thursday.
lines: The cloud is coming over the mountain like it pays rent here.
That cloud will be down on the streetlights before the walk is done.
Low cloud at night keeps the cold off the promenade, and the regulars know it.

images.seen: A man in slops standing beside his mower on a half-mowed lawn, looking up at a heavy grey sky over the mountain, beer waiting on the patio table. Saturday.
lines: Half a lawn mowed, and now the negotiation with the sky begins.
The sky is deciding whether the second half of that lawn happens today.
That look is a man asking the clouds for forty-five more minutes.

images.seen: A woman jogging along the Umhlanga promenade past the whalebone pier arches, pearly overcast sky over a warm grey sea, her ponytail lifting in the breeze. Sunday.
lines: Durban grey is still twenty-four degrees, which is why the promenade never empties.
The cloud is doing sunscreen duty this morning and the runners are cashing in.
A pearl-grey sky and a warm sea breeze: the coast's version of mild.

images.seen: A man standing on his tiled roof beside new solar panels, hands on hips, giving a fully grey sky a skeptical look. Tuesday.
lines: Panels installed, sun absent: the sky owes this roof an apology.
Grey from gutter to gutter, and every kilowatt up here is on standby.
The forecast said partly sunny; the sky went with fully committed grey.
